title: Models, Laws, Theories, and Chemistry Decisions
purpose: Distinguish models, laws, theories, and chemistry-based decisions.
labDataRequirement: Model/law/theory comparison and chemistry decision evidence using case scenarios.
safetyNotes: Use written case evidence only. Do not test consumer products or chemicals without assignment.
simulationReview: Direct simulation/resource link is provided in P01.html and in directSimulationUrl.
assessmentStimulusNeeded: Use the Unit 1 matrix requirement for this lesson: embedded scenario, table, graph, model, diagram, or organizer as needed.
simulationVirtualLabReviewRequirement: Required for safety/procedure practice, measurement/data analysis, and particle models
simulationVirtualLabReviewFocus: Model/law/theory comparison and chemistry decision evidence
directSimulationStudentTask: After the simulation opens, start with the atom model shown on the screen and turn on alpha-particle firing if it is not already moving. Observe several alpha particles and separate their paths into mostly straight, slightly deflected, or strongly deflected. Switch or compare available atom-model views if the simulation provides more than one model. Record which observation supports a small dense nucleus and one limitation of the model for the lesson focus: Models, Laws, Theories, and Chemistry Decisions.
simulationReviewImplementation: Student-facing lesson includes one exact direct simulation/resource link plus adjacent step-by-step directions for what to open, click/use, observe, record, and connect to the lesson standard.
simulationSourceReference: CPALMS resources; ACS chemistry in society resources
